Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! India Women players are in a huddle before spreading out and taking their respective field positions. Georgia Voll and Beth Mooney are the two openers for Australia Women. Renuka Singh Thakur to start proceedings with the ball. Also, Richa Ghosh, the keeper, is upto the stumps. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

A tough task ahead - The Aussies will feel 177 is a gettable score on this wicket but it will need some chasing. Their bowlers were inconsistent at best and those one-over spells didn't quite work out for Sophie Molineux. Every bowler went for around 8 to 9 runs an over in terms of economy but no one built any sort of consistent pressure on the batters. Annabel Sutherland certainly delivered a magnificent final over, but was that enough? Only time will tell. Stay tuned as the run chase is up next.

Runs on the board - The Indian skipper, Harmanpreet Kaur, mentioned at the toss about putting a good total on the board and that's exactly what India have done. After losing Shafali Verma early, it turned into the Smriti-Jemi show for India. Jemimah Rodrigues played the cheeky shots and got out off the blocks quickly as Smriti Mandhana just kept raising her game up a notch and accelerated all throughout her inning. The duo ruled the middle phase but soon enough, Rodrigues struggled to find the boundaries and it was up to Mandhana to throw caution to the wind. She did hit plenty of boundaries, including some big ones as well but fell for 82. Rodrigues also notched up a fifty as Richa Ghosh made a quickfire 18 before the last over completely sucked the momentum out of the innings.

Enough of a comeback? A good, fighting comeback from the Aussies at the death and that final over from Annabel Sutherland will certainly give them some momentum. However, India Women will feel the damage had already been done in the middle phase of the innings, thanks to that huge 121-run stand between Smriti Mandhana and Jemimah Rodrigues.

OUT! DEEPTI SHARMA IS RUN OUT! Annabel Sutherland bowls a slower delivery, fuller and on the fifth stump. Deepti Sharma leans forward to reach the pitched area of the delivery and tries to swat it across, but ends up hitting from the toe end. The ball loops and drops safely in the vacant wide mid on region. Ellyse Perry sprints from the boundary ropes and throws it to the keeper's end as she spots Sharma struggling to get the second run. The rest is done by Beth Mooney. Despite the dive, Deepti Sharma fell short of reaching her home. India Women ended their inning posting 176 runs on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin! The umpires are out in the middle and the Aussies make their way through the fireworks and spread out onto the field. It will be the duo of Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma to open the innings for India Women. Darcie Brown has the new ball in hand and she's raring to go. It seems like there's a fair bit of live grass on the pitch as well. A single slip in place, let's go...

India Women (Playing XI) - Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Amanjot Kaur, Arundhati Reddy, Shreyanka Patil (In for Kranti Gaud), Sree Charani, and Renuka Singh Thakur.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Georgia Voll, Beth Mooney (WK), Phoebe Litchfield, Ellyse Perry, Ashleigh Gardner, Georgia Wareham, Annabel Sutherland, Grace Harris (In for Nicola Carey), Sophie Molineux (C), Kim Garth, and Darcie Brown.

The Australia Women skipper - Sophie Molineux says that they would have bowled first anyway. Adds that they want to continue from where they left off in the last game. Mentions that she loved how their bowlers stuck it out in the last game, they knew that India would come hard but they didn't panic. Says that she is loving her time as a captain, the girls and the management have been great and supportive. On Ellyse Perry playing in her 350th international game, she calls her a legend and says her contribution to the game has been priceless and she deserves this moment. It will be great to win against India on this special occasion. Informs that Nicola Carey is not playing and Grace Harris comes in for her, it is purely on the basis of tinkering with the balance of the team.

The captain of India Women - Harmanpreet Kaur says that they will look to put a good total on the board and enjoy the game. About their last match, she says that in batting, they should have concentrated on building partnerships. She hopes that her bowling unit will provide the same performance they gave in the last two matches. Ends up saying that they have one change in the playing XI as Shreyanka Patil comes in for Kranti Gaud.

TOSS - It's toss time in Adelaide and thankfully, the conditions look sunny. Harmanpreet Kaur and Sophie Molineux are out in the middle and it is the former who calls it correctly. India Women will BAT first.

Weather might be a problem - The anticipation is growing to get the T20I series decider underway between these two champion sides, but according to the weather forecast, there is a slight 20-25 percent chance of passing showers developing in the evening. Let's hope we get a full match without any interruption. Stick around for the toss and further updates.

One step away from glory - India Women will be eager to reclaim the dominance they showed in the series opener, where they dismantled the Australian lineup to win by 21 runs via the DLS method. The visitors have found a hero in Arundhati Reddy, who has been the pick of the bowlers with a career best of 4/22 in the first game, followed by another strong performance to pull 2 wickets in the latest encounter. For India to secure a historic series win on Australian soil, they will need their key batters to hold their nerve during the frantic death overs that cost them in the previous match.

Molineux's first win - Australia Women enter this decider with renewed confidence after a clinical bounce-back performance in the second T20I. Despite a shaky start to the series under new captain Sophie Molineux, the world No. 1 side displayed its trademark resilience to level the score with a 19-run victory. The standout performer has undoubtedly been Georgia Voll, whose explosive 88 off 57 in the second match proved why she is one of the game's rising stars. Supporting her has been the reliable Ashleigh Gardner, who snared three wickets to stifle the Indian chase, and veteran Beth Mooney, whose consistency at the top-order in the batting unit remains a cornerstone for the hosts.

Welcome, folks - The stage is set for a high-stakes finale in the three-match T20I series between Australia Women and India Women. With the series currently deadlocked at 1-1, this third and final encounter is no longer just a game, it is a 'winner takes it all' showdown. Both heavyweights have traded blows across Sydney and Canberra, and now they descend upon Adelaide to decide who will hoist the trophy and claim the ultimate momentum heading into the upcoming ODI leg of the tour.
... MATCH DAY ...

Series at level footing - With the T20I series currently deadlocked at 1-1, this final clash serves as the thrilling climax to the shortest format before the tour transitions into three ODIs and a one-off Test. As both teams are presently level on 2 points in this multi-format series, the winner at Adelaide will seize a critical advantage in the overall standings, heading into the ODI series with 4 points to their name.  A tale of two games - The series opener in Sydney was a rain-marred affair that saw India draw first blood. India's bowlers restricted the world-ranked No. 1 Australians to just 133. India won by 21 runs (DLS method) after rain halted their chase at 50/1. Australia, however, roared back in the second T20I at Canberra. Young opener Georgia Voll struck a brilliant 88 to propel the hosts to 163/5. Despite a solid start from Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma, India suffered a late-innings collapse, losing six wickets in quick succession, which led to a 19-run defeat. Strengths and weaknesses - Australia Women have showcased their trademark depth and resilience. Their greatest strength remains their top-order batting and the emergence of fresh talent like Georgia Voll, who successfully anchored the innings in Canberra. However, they have shown vulnerability under pressure, particularly in the first game, where their world-class batting unit crumbled against disciplined Indian pace. India Women have relied heavily on their bowling attack and explosive opening pair. Arundhati Reddy has been the standout performer of the tour so far, taking 6 wickets across two matches. Their primary weakness is a fragile middle order, and the inability to close out the chase in Canberra highlighted a recurring struggle to maintain momentum once the openers are dismissed. Form (Last 5 completed T20Is, most recent first) - Australia - WLWWW | India - LWWWW. Crucial aspects - As the teams head to Adelaide, the Powerplay battle will likely be the series-defining factor. If Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana can survive the initial burst and capitalize on the field restrictions, India will be well-placed to handle the Australian spinners later on. For Australia, the key will be Ashleigh Gardner’s all-round contribution as her three-wicket haul in the second game proved that her middle-over breakthroughs can derail even the most settled Indian partnerships.
